messages.subject: vector operator/(vector x, real y)
parts:
Imagine a data block like:
data { ...; vector[N] x; ...; }
and a transformed data block like:
transformed data { vector[N] x100; ... ; }

vector operator*(vector x, real y) is documented, and
x100 <- x * 100.0;
is compiled.

vector operator/(vector x, real y) is not documented, but
x100 <- x / 100.0;
is compiled too. It's convenient, even if one could easily write x * 0.01.

However, since "Stan automatically promotes integer values to real values if necessary" (page 143), I've also tried:

x100 <- x * 100;
x100 <- x / 100;

I was sure that, as vectors always contain real values, "100" would be automatically promoted to "100.0", but I've got a very long and confusing (to me, at least) error message. Not even

x100 <- x * 100 * 1.0;
x100 <- x / 100 * 1.0;

(where I hoped "* 1.0" would "force" the promotion to real) work.

Perhaps the vector operator/(vector x, real y) could be documented and the missed promotion to real could be fixed or documented.
I attach a model and the corresponding error message.

HTH

Sergio

messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] vector operator/(vector x, real y)
parts:
I actually ran into this same error, but the bug (x / 100 not working)
has been fixed for 2.0, so now with 2.0, x / 100 should not throw errors
and will work fine. And I just checked the manual draft in the dev repo,
the signatures operator/ and operator* for (vector,real), (matrix,real),
(row vector,real) are all present.


Peter
